newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bank sector hurt by renewed sales.
newsitem.headline: Japan bank sector hurt by renewed sales.

text.p: Shares in Japan's banking sector were dragged down on Monday afternoon by dimmer earnings forecasts and vague market rumours about fresh financial troubles at some Japanese banks, brokers said.
The banking sector was ranked as the top percentage loser on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
Mitsubishi Trust & Banking Corp was down 110 yen at 1,140 yen by 0501 GMT.
Shares in Chuo Trust & Banking Co Ltd were down 58 yen at 732 yen, while Yasuda Trust & Banking Co Ltd was down 28 yen at 365 yen.
Shares in Fuji Bank Ltd shed 110 yen to 1,190 yen, and Daiwa Bank Ltd was down 35 yen at 474 yen.
Brokers said vague rumours were circulated in the market that some Japanese banks may be suffering losses from derivatives trading and these spurred sales of shares in the banking sector.

Adding to the sector's gloomy mood was a mid-afternoon announcement by Moody's Investors Service that it had lowered its ratings outlook for Nippon Credit Bank Ltd, Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd, Yasuda Trust & Banking and Chuo Trust & Banking to negative from stable.
